items.prompt: On a map grid, a hiking trail runs straight from campsite A(−2, 6) to campsite B(8, −4). A water station is built at the midpoint of the trail. What are the coordinates of the water station?

wrong.why: Added the coordinates but forgot to divide by 2.
Found half the difference of the coordinates instead of half the sum.
Dropped the negative sign on −4 when averaging the y-coordinates: (6 + 4)/2 = 5.

items.prompt: The midpoint of segment AB is M(3, −1). Endpoint A is (7, 2). What are the coordinates of endpoint B?

wrong.why: Averaged M and A instead of using M as the average of A and B.
Added the coordinates of M and A.
Subtracted A from M without doubling: (3 − 7, −1 − 2).

items.explanation: Since M is the average of A and B: 3 = (7 + x)/2 gives x = −1, and −1 = (2 + y)/2 gives y = −4.

items.prompt: The midpoint of segment PQ is (4, −1). Point P is (a, 2) and point Q is (10, b). What is the value of a + b?

wrong.why: Dropped the negative signs of a and b.
Found only a.

items.prompt: Parallelogram ABCD has vertices A(1, 1), B(5, 2) and C(7, 6), listed in order around the figure. What are the coordinates of D?

wrong.why: Used B + C − A, the fourth vertex of a different parallelogram.
Used A + B − C, the fourth vertex of a different parallelogram.
Stopped at the midpoint of diagonal AC instead of using it to find D.

items.explanation: Diagonals of a parallelogram share a midpoint. Midpoint of AC is (4, 3.5), so D = 2(4, 3.5) − B = (3, 5).

items.prompt: Which equation describes the line parallel to y = 2x − 3 that passes through the point (4, 1)?

wrong.why: Used the perpendicular slope −1/2.
Used the y-coordinate of the point as the y-intercept.
Changed the sign of the slope instead of keeping it.

items.explanation: Parallel lines share slope 2. Then 1 = 2(4) + b gives b = −7, so y = 2x − 7.

items.prompt: Which equation describes the line perpendicular to y = 3x + 1 that passes through the point (6, 1)?

wrong.why: Flipped the slope to 1/3 but did not make it negative.
Changed only the sign of the slope and did not take the reciprocal.
Used the same slope, which gives a parallel line.

items.explanation: The perpendicular slope is −1/3. Then 1 = −(1/3)(6) + b gives b = 3, so y = −x/3 + 3.

items.prompt: Line 1 passes through (1, 2) and (5, 10). Line 2 is x + 2y = 6. How are the two lines related?
items.answer: Perpendicular: slopes 2 and −1/2

wrong.text: Parallel: both slopes are 2
wrong.why: Read the slope of line 2 as the coefficient of y.

wrong.text: Neither: slopes 2 and 1/2
wrong.why: Dropped the negative sign when rewriting line 2 as y = −x/2 + 3.

wrong.text: Neither: slopes 2 and −2
wrong.why: Took the slope of line 2 as the negative of the y-coefficient.

items.explanation: Line 1 has slope (10 − 2)/(5 − 1) = 2. Line 2 is y = −x/2 + 3, slope −1/2. The slopes are negative reciprocals, so the lines are perpendicular.

items.prompt: Which equation describes the line parallel to 3x − 2y = 8 that passes through (−2, 5)?

wrong.why: Read the slope as 3, the coefficient of x, without solving for y.
Used the perpendicular slope −2/3.
Got the sign of the slope wrong when solving for y.

items.explanation: Solving gives y = (3/2)x − 4, so the slope is 3/2. Then 5 = (3/2)(−2) + b gives b = 8.

items.prompt: Line 1 is y = (2/3)x + 1. Line 2 is 3x + ky = 5. For what value of k are the two lines perpendicular?
items.explanation: Line 2 has slope −3/k. Perpendicular means (2/3)(−3/k) = −1, so −2/k = −1 and k = 2.

wrong.why: Set the slopes equal (parallel) instead of negative reciprocals.
Set −3/k equal to 3/2 without the correct sign.

items.prompt: A rectangular garden has corners at (1, 2), (8, 2), (8, 5) and (1, 5) on a coordinate grid where each unit is 1 meter. What is its area?
items.answer: 21 square meters

wrong.text: 20 square meters
wrong.why: Found the perimeter, 2(7 + 3), instead of the area.

wrong.text: 10 square meters
wrong.why: Added the side lengths 7 + 3.

wrong.text: 24 square meters
wrong.why: Used the x-coordinate 8 as the length instead of 8 − 1 = 7.

items.explanation: Length = 8 − 1 = 7 and width = 5 − 2 = 3, so area = 7 × 3 = 21.

items.prompt: A triangle has vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (6, 8). What is its perimeter in units?
items.explanation: The legs are 6 and 8. The hypotenuse is √(6² + 8²) = 10. Perimeter = 6 + 8 + 10 = 24.

wrong.why: Added only the two legs.
Gave only the hypotenuse.

items.prompt: A triangle has vertices (0, 0), (8, 0) and (3, 5). What is its area in square units?

wrong.why: Forgot the factor 1/2 in the area formula.
Used the x-coordinate 3 of the top vertex as the height.
Added the base 8 and the height 5.

items.explanation: The base along the x-axis is 8 and the height is 5. Area = (1/2)(8)(5) = 20.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, 0), B(4, 0) and C(2, 5). Which description is correct?
items.answer: Isosceles, but not equilateral

wrong.text: Equilateral
wrong.why: Saw that AC = BC and assumed all three sides must match.

wrong.text: Right isosceles
wrong.why: Assumed a right angle at C without checking the slopes.

wrong.text: Scalene
wrong.why: Compared the base 4 with 2 + 5 and never noticed AC = BC.

items.explanation: AB = 4. AC = √(2² + 5²) = √29 and BC = √(2² + 5²) = √29. Two sides are equal and the third is 4, so the triangle is isosceles. The slopes of AC and BC are 5/2 and −5/2, whose product is not −1, so no right angle.

items.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD has vertices A(−1, 2), B(2, 4), C(4, 1) and D(1, −1). Which name fits it best?
items.answer: Square

wrong.text: Rectangle that is not a square
wrong.why: Checked the slopes for right angles but never compared the side lengths.

wrong.text: Rhombus that is not a square
wrong.why: Found four equal sides but did not check the slopes for right angles.

wrong.text: Parallelogram that is not a rectangle
wrong.why: Verified opposite sides are parallel and stopped.

items.explanation: Each side has length √13, and slopes 2/3 and −3/2 for adjacent sides are negative reciprocals, so the angles are right angles. Four equal sides plus right angles make a square.

items.prompt: A triangle has vertices (1, 1), (7, 3) and (4, 8). What is its area in square units?

wrong.why: Added the areas of the three corner triangles instead of subtracting them.
Computed twice the area (the parallelogram) and did not halve it.
Gave the area of the bounding rectangle, 6 × 7.

items.explanation: The bounding rectangle is 6 × 7 = 42. Subtract the corner triangles: 6 + 7.5 + 10.5 = 24. Area = 42 − 24 = 18.

items.prompt: A histogram shows the points scored by 20 students on a quiz, in intervals of width 10: 0–9 has 6 students, 10–19 has 3, 20–29 has 5, 30–39 has 4 and 40–49 has 2. How many students scored below 20 points?

wrong.why: Counted only the first bar.
Counted only the 10–19 bar.
Also counted the 20–29 bar.

items.explanation: Add the bars for 0–9 and 10–19: 6 + 3 = 9.

items.prompt: A histogram shows the commute time, in minutes, of 24 students. The intervals and counts are 0–9: 7, 10–19: 3, 20–29: 6, 30–39: 5, 40–49: 3. Which interval contains the median commute time?

wrong.why: Picked the tallest bar, which shows the mode, not the median.
Counted to half of 20 values (10) instead of half of 24, and stopped one bar early.
Took the median of the bar heights (5) instead of locating the middle value.

items.explanation: With 24 values the median is the average of the 12th and 13th. Running totals are 7, 10, 16, so both lie in 20–29.

items.prompt: To draw a box plot, a student orders these 11 values: 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 15, 15, 18, 20, 26. Using the median-of-halves method (leave out the median when the count is odd), what is the five-number summary (min, Q1, median, Q3, max)?

wrong.why: Kept the median in both halves when finding the quartiles.
Used the midpoint of the minimum and maximum as the median.
Placed the quartiles a quarter and three-quarters of the way from the minimum to the maximum.

items.explanation: The median is the 6th value, 13. Lower half 4, 7, 8, 10, 12 has median 8. Upper half 15, 15, 18, 20, 26 has median 18.

items.prompt: A box plot of daily steps (in hundreds) has five-number summary: minimum 12, Q1 20, median 26, Q3 40, maximum 58. About what percent of the days had values between the median (26) and Q3 (40)?

wrong.why: Used the span from Q1 to Q3, which holds the middle half of the data.
Used the span from the minimum up to Q3.
Subtracted 40 − 26 and read the difference as a percent.

items.explanation: Each section of a box plot (min to Q1, Q1 to median, median to Q3, Q3 to max) holds about 25% of the data.

items.prompt: Find the interquartile range (IQR) of these values using the median-of-halves method: 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 19.
items.explanation: The lower half 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 has median 6. The upper half 11, 12, 14, 15, 19 has median 14. IQR = 14 − 6 = 8.

wrong.why: Gave the range, 19 − 3.
Gave the median of the whole data set.

items.prompt: Two classes took the same exam. Class A has median 78 and IQR 6. Class B has median 78 and IQR 18. Which statement is best supported?
items.answer: Class A's scores are more consistent, because its IQR is smaller.

wrong.text: Class B's scores are more consistent, because its IQR is larger.
wrong.why: Believed a larger IQR means more consistency.

wrong.text: Class B scored higher overall, because its IQR is larger.
wrong.why: Read a larger IQR as better performance.

wrong.text: The classes have the same spread, because the medians are equal.
wrong.why: Used the equal medians to judge spread.

items.explanation: The IQR measures spread. A smaller IQR means the middle half of the scores are closer together, while the equal medians show the typical score is the same.

items.prompt: A histogram of household incomes in a town is strongly skewed to the right. Which pair of statistics best describes the center and spread?
items.answer: Median and IQR

wrong.text: Mean and standard deviation
wrong.why: Used mean and SD for every shape, although the long tail pulls both.

wrong.text: Mean and IQR
wrong.why: Mixed a measure affected by outliers with one that is not.

wrong.text: Median and range
wrong.why: Paired the median with the range, which depends entirely on the extreme values.

items.explanation: For skewed data, the median and IQR resist the pull of the long tail, so they describe the typical value and spread better.

items.prompt: Set P is 10, 10, 11, 11, 12. Set Q is 4, 8, 11, 14, 18. Which set has the larger standard deviation, and why?
items.answer: Set Q: its values are farther from its mean

wrong.text: Set P: its values are closer together
wrong.why: Thought tightly packed values mean a larger standard deviation.

wrong.text: Set P: several of its values repeat
wrong.why: Treated repeated values as a sign of more variation.

wrong.text: Neither: the means are nearly equal
wrong.why: Assumed similar means force similar standard deviations.

items.explanation: Both means are about 11. Set P's values stay within 1 of the mean, while Set Q's are 3 to 7 away, so Set Q is more spread out and has the larger standard deviation.

items.prompt: Two bike shops recorded repair times in days. Shop A: min 2, Q1 4, median 6, Q3 9, max 14. Shop B: min 1, Q1 5, median 6, Q3 7, max 20. Which statement is supported by the data?
items.answer: The medians match, but Shop A's middle 50% is more spread out.

wrong.text: Shop B's middle 50% is more spread out, because its range is larger.
wrong.why: Uses the range (which is affected by extreme values) to judge the spread of the middle half of the data.

wrong.text: Shop A is faster, because its Q3 is larger.
wrong.why: Read a larger Q3 as better, when longer repair times are worse.

wrong.text: Shop B is faster, because its minimum is lower.
wrong.why: Compared minimums instead of the medians, which are equal.

items.explanation: Both medians are 6. The IQR is 5 for Shop A and 2 for Shop B, so Shop A's middle half is more spread out even though Shop B has the larger range (19 vs 12).

items.prompt: For the data 4, 6, 6, 8, 21, find the mean minus the median.
items.explanation: Mean = 45/5 = 9. Median = 6. Mean − median = 3.

wrong.why: Subtracted in the wrong order.
Gave only the mean.

items.prompt: The values 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 have mean 14 and median 14. A new value, 60, is added. What are the new mean and median?
items.answer: Mean 21.7, median 14.5

wrong.text: Mean 14.5, median 21.7
wrong.why: Swapped which statistic is pulled by the outlier.

wrong.text: Mean 37, median 14.5
wrong.why: Averaged the old mean with the new value instead of using all six values.

wrong.text: Mean 21.7, median 15
wrong.why: Took the upper middle value instead of averaging the two middle values.

items.explanation: New mean = (70 + 60)/6 ≈ 21.7. The six ordered values have middle values 14 and 15, so the median is 14.5. The mean moves a lot; the median barely moves.

items.prompt: A data set has median 30, Q1 = 24 and Q3 = 36. Its extreme values are 4, 8, 50 and 58. Using the rule that outliers lie more than 1.5 × IQR below Q1 or above Q3, which values are outliers?
items.answer: 4 and 58

wrong.text: 58 only
wrong.why: Checked only the upper fence and ignored the lower one.
Used 1 × IQR instead of 1.5 × IQR for the fences.

wrong.text: 50 and 58
wrong.why: Measured 1.5 × IQR up from the median (30 + 18 = 48) and ignored the lower fence.

items.explanation: IQR = 12 and 1.5 × IQR = 18. The fences are 24 − 18 = 6 and 36 + 18 = 54. Only 4 (below 6) and 58 (above 54) fall outside.

items.prompt: The five values 10, 12, 13, 14, 16 are joined by a sixth value, 40. Using the median-of-halves method, what is the IQR of the six values?
items.explanation: Ordered: 10, 12, 13, 14, 16, 40. The lower half 10, 12, 13 has median 12; the upper half 14, 16, 40 has median 16. IQR = 16 − 12 = 4. The outlier changes the range a lot but not the IQR.

wrong.why: Gave the range, 40 − 10.
Subtracted Q1 from the outlier, 40 − 12.

items.prompt: Seven home prices, in thousands of dollars, are 210, 220, 225, 230, 240, 250 and 900. Which is the best choice for a typical price, and why?
items.answer: $230 thousand, the median, which resists the $900 thousand outlier

wrong.text: $325 thousand, the mean, because it uses every value
wrong.why: Used the mean even though the outlier pulls it far above most prices.

wrong.text: $555 thousand, halfway between the lowest and highest price
wrong.why: Used the midrange, which is driven entirely by the outlier.

wrong.text: $235 thousand, the average of the 4th and 5th values
wrong.why: Treated the 7 values as an even count and averaged two middle values.

items.explanation: The mean is 2275/7 = 325, pulled up by the 900. The median is the 4th value, 230, and is a better description of a typical home.

items.prompt: The mean of 10 commute times is 18.4 minutes. One time is an outlier. After it is removed, the mean of the remaining 9 times is 15.0 minutes. What was the outlier, in minutes?

wrong.why: Subtracted the two means, 18.4 − 15.0.
Multiplied 15.0 by 10 instead of 9 before subtracting.
Added the two means, 18.4 + 15.0.

items.explanation: Total of all 10 = 10 × 18.4 = 184. Total of the other 9 = 9 × 15.0 = 135. Outlier = 184 − 135 = 49.

items.prompt: A student records hours of screen time per day (x) and hours of sleep (y) for six classmates: (1, 9.0), (2, 8.6), (3, 8.4), (4, 7.7), (5, 7.4), (6, 6.9). How are the variables related?
items.answer: A strong negative linear association

wrong.text: A strong positive linear association
wrong.why: Read the downward trend as upward.

wrong.text: No association
wrong.why: Saw small changes in y and concluded there was no pattern.

wrong.text: A strong exponential growth pattern
wrong.why: Mistook a steady drop for a curve that grows.

items.explanation: As screen time rises, sleep falls steadily by roughly 0.45 hour per extra hour, so the association is negative and linear.

items.prompt: A scatter plot has the points (0, 3), (1, 6), (2, 12), (3, 24) and (4, 48). Which description fits the pattern best?
items.answer: Exponential growth: y doubles as x increases by 1

wrong.text: Linear growth: y rises about 11 for each step
wrong.why: Averaged the change over all steps and ignored that the increases keep growing.

wrong.text: Linear growth: y rises 3 for each step in x
wrong.why: Used the first y-value as the constant increase.

wrong.text: Exponential decay: y halves as x increases by 1
wrong.why: Read the doubling ratio backward.

items.explanation: The increases (3, 6, 12, 24) are not constant, but each y is 2 times the previous one, so the pattern is exponential growth.

items.prompt: The least-squares line for hours studied per week (x) and quiz score (y) is ŷ = 3.5x + 48. For what number of hours does the line predict a score of 83?
items.explanation: Solve 3.5x + 48 = 83. Then 3.5x = 35 and x = 10.

wrong.why: Subtracted 48 but did not divide by 3.5.
Added 48 instead of subtracting it: (83 + 48)/3.5.

items.prompt: The least-squares line for a used car's age in years (x) and its value in dollars (y) is ŷ = −1500x + 24000. What value does the line predict for a 6-year-old car?

wrong.why: Subtracted only one year's loss, 24,000 − 1,500.
Added 1,500 × 6 instead of subtracting it.
Multiplied 1,500 × 6 and forgot the 24,000.

items.prompt: A line of best fit is ŷ = 1.5x + 8. At x = 10 the actual data value is y = 21. What is the residual (actual − predicted)?
items.explanation: Predicted ŷ = 1.5(10) + 8 = 23. Residual = 21 − 23 = −2.

wrong.why: Subtracted in the wrong order (predicted − actual).
Gave the predicted value.

items.prompt: A line is fit to data at x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The residuals (actual − predicted) are 6, 1, −3, −4, −3, 0, 3. What do they suggest?
items.answer: A U-shaped pattern, so a line is not a good model

wrong.text: They add to 0, so a line fits well
wrong.why: Treated a zero total as proof of fit, but least-squares residuals always add to 0.

wrong.text: Some are small, so a line fits well
wrong.why: Judged fit from a few small residuals and ignored the pattern.

wrong.text: The line is too steep, so the slope should be lowered
wrong.why: Mistook a curved residual pattern for a slope error.

items.explanation: The residuals go positive, then negative, then positive again. A random scatter would support a line; this curved pattern shows the data are curved.

items.prompt: Points (1, 3), (2, 5) and (3, 8) are compared with two lines. Model A: ŷ = 2.5x + 0.5. Model B: ŷ = 2x + 1. Which model has the smaller sum of squared residuals, and what are the two sums?
items.answer: Model A: 0.25 versus 1 for Model B

wrong.text: Model A: 0.5 versus 1 for Model B
wrong.why: Added the residuals' sizes without squaring the −0.5.

wrong.text: Model B: 1 versus 0.25 for Model A
wrong.why: Matched the sums correctly but picked the larger one as better.

wrong.text: Model B: 0 versus 0.25 for Model A
wrong.why: Counted only B's zero residuals and overlooked its residual of 1.

items.explanation: Model A predicts 3, 5.5, 8, with residuals 0, −0.5, 0 and sum of squares 0.25. Model B predicts 3, 5, 7, with residuals 0, 0, 1 and sum of squares 1. The smaller sum is the better fit.

items.prompt: An exponential model for a bacteria colony is B = 50(2)^t, where t is hours and B is the number of bacteria. What number does it predict at t = 4?

wrong.why: Multiplied 50 × 2 × 4 instead of using 2 as a repeated factor.
Multiplied 50 × 4.
Used 2^5 instead of 2^4.

items.prompt: An exponential model for the rebound height (cm) of a ball is ŷ = 120(0.9)^x, where x is the bounce number. What height does the model predict for x = 2?

wrong.why: Used the factor 0.9 only once.
Multiplied 120 × 0.9 × 2.

items.prompt: The least-squares line ŷ = 2.4x + 15 predicts the number of free throws made out of 50 (y) from weekly practice hours (x). What does the slope 2.4 mean?
items.answer: Each extra practice hour adds about 2.4 predicted free throws.

wrong.text: A player who never practices is predicted to make 2.4 shots.
wrong.why: Mixed up the slope with the intercept.

wrong.text: Each extra practice hour adds about 15 predicted free throws.
wrong.why: Used the intercept as the rate of change.

wrong.text: Each extra free throw made adds about 2.4 practice hours.
wrong.why: Reversed the roles of the variables.

items.explanation: The slope is the change in predicted y for each 1-unit increase in x, here 2.4 free throws per hour.

items.prompt: A seedling's height in cm (y) is modeled by ŷ = 1.8x + 4, where x is the number of days since the first measurement. What does the intercept 4 represent?
items.answer: The predicted height at the first measurement (day 0)

wrong.text: The number of centimeters gained each day
wrong.why: Mixed up the intercept with the slope.

wrong.text: The predicted height on the fourth day
wrong.why: Treated 4 as a value of x instead of a value of y.

wrong.text: The number of days until the seedling stops growing
wrong.why: Gave the intercept a meaning that has nothing to do with the model.

items.explanation: The intercept is ŷ when x = 0, so it is the predicted starting height: 4 cm.

items.prompt: The line ŷ = 3.2x + 52 was fit to test scores (y, out of 100) for students who studied from 0 to 8 hours (x). A student plans to study 20 hours. Which evaluation is best?
items.answer: Predicts 116, which is not valid: 20 is far outside the data and scores top out at 100.

wrong.text: Predicts 116, which is valid: a line works for any number of hours studied.
wrong.why: Assumed a linear model can be extended without limit.

wrong.text: Predicts 116, which is valid: studying more always raises a score.
wrong.why: Treated the trend as unlimited instead of noticing the 100-point maximum.

wrong.text: Predicts 64, which is a reasonable value for a score, so the model is fine.
wrong.why: Forgot to add the intercept 52.

items.explanation: ŷ = 3.2(20) + 52 = 116. That is extrapolation well beyond the 0 to 8 hour data, and a score over 100 is impossible, so the prediction is not trustworthy.

items.prompt: The correlation between daily hours of TV watched and test score for a group of students is r = −0.85. Which interpretation is correct?
items.answer: A strong negative linear relationship

wrong.text: A strong positive linear relationship
wrong.why: Ignored the sign and saw only that 0.85 is close to 1.

wrong.text: 85% of students who watch TV score lower
wrong.why: Read r as a percent of students.

wrong.text: A weak negative linear relationship
wrong.why: Read −0.85 as a small number because of the minus sign.

items.explanation: r is between −1 and 1. Its sign gives the direction (negative) and its size gives the strength (0.85 is close to 1, so strong).

items.prompt: A scatter plot looks curved. A line fit to the data has r = 0.93, but its residual plot shows a clear U shape. What is the best conclusion?
items.answer: A line is not appropriate even though r is high; a curve fits better.

wrong.text: A line is appropriate for these data, because r is close to 1.
wrong.why: Used r alone and ignored the residual pattern.

wrong.text: 93% of the points lie exactly on the fitted line.
wrong.why: Read r as the percent of points on the line.

wrong.text: The U shape shows that the correlation must be negative, not positive.
wrong.why: Mistook a residual pattern for the sign of r.

items.explanation: A high r only measures how close the data are to a line overall. A patterned residual plot shows a systematic misfit, so a nonlinear model is better.

items.prompt: Over 30 summer days, a beach town finds that daily ice cream sales and daily sunburn cases have a correlation of r = 0.88. Which conclusion is best supported?
items.answer: Both rise on hot, sunny days; the data do not show that one causes the other.

wrong.text: Ice cream sales cause people to get sunburns.
wrong.why: Treated a strong correlation as proof that one variable causes the other.

wrong.text: Sunburns cause people to buy more ice cream cones.
wrong.why: Reversed the cause and effect, still assuming causation.

wrong.text: The strong correlation proves that no other factor is involved at all.
wrong.why: Believed a high r rules out a lurking variable.

items.explanation: A hidden factor, hot sunny weather, can drive both variables. Correlation shows association, not causation.
